words.notes: To agree with a negative question, Germans use doch instead of ja: 'Hast du keinen Hunger?' — 'Doch!' (Yes, I am hungry).

cloze.en: — Would you like anything else? — No, thank you.

words.notes: 'Nein, danke' is the polite way to decline anything. Just 'nein' on its own can sound blunt.

example_sentences.de: Ich verstehe nicht, was Sie meinen.
example_sentences.en: I don't understand what you mean.

cloze.de: Tut mir leid, ich ___ nicht. Können Sie das wiederholen?
cloze.en: Sorry, I don't understand. Can you repeat that?

words.notes: Possibly the most useful sentence you will learn. Follow it with 'Können Sie das bitte wiederholen?'

example_sentences.de: Entschuldigung, können Sie das bitte wiederholen?
example_sentences.en: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?

example_sentences.de: Können Sie das bitte noch einmal wiederholen?
example_sentences.en: Could you please repeat that once more?

cloze.de: Das ging zu schnell. Können Sie das bitte ___?
cloze.en: That was too fast. Could you repeat that, please?

words.notes: With friends use the du form: 'Kannst du das bitte wiederholen?'

words.translation: Could you speak more slowly, please?
translations: Could you speak more slowly, please?

example_sentences.de: Können Sie bitte langsamer sprechen? Ich lerne noch Deutsch.
example_sentences.en: Could you speak more slowly, please? I'm still learning German.
Please speak a little more slowly.

cloze.en: Could you speak more slowly, please?

words.notes: Germans genuinely speak fast. Saying this early in a conversation saves a lot of confusion later.

example_sentences.en: Excuse me, do you speak English?

cloze.en: Excuse me, do you speak English?

words.germany_context: Most Germans under 40 speak decent English, but at the Bürgeramt, with older tradespeople and in rural areas, expect German only. Trying in German first is always appreciated.

words.translation: I only speak a little German.
translations: I only speak a little German.

example_sentences.de: Ich spreche nur wenig Deutsch, bitte langsam.
example_sentences.en: I only speak a little German, slowly please.

example_sentences.de: Mein Deutsch ist noch nicht gut.

cloze.en: I only speak a little German.

words.notes: Saying this up front makes people slow down and simplify. It works far better than staying silent.

example_sentences.de: Ich lerne seit drei Monaten Deutsch.
example_sentences.en: I've been learning German for three months.

example_sentences.de: Ich lerne Deutsch, aber es ist schwer.
example_sentences.en: I'm learning German, but it's hard.

cloze.en: I've been learning German for a year.

words.notes: Note German uses the present tense with seit for something still going on: 'Ich lerne seit drei Monaten' = 'I have been learning for three months'.

example_sentences.de: Wie bitte? Das habe ich nicht verstanden.
Wie bitte? Können Sie lauter sprechen?

cloze.de: ___ bitte? Ich habe Sie nicht gehört.

words.notes: The standard polite 'I didn't catch that'. Saying just 'Was?' sounds rude to strangers.

words.word: Wie sagt man das auf Deutsch?
words.lemma: Wie sagt man das auf Deutsch
words.translation: How do you say that in German?
translations: How do you say that in German?

example_sentences.de: Wie sagt man das auf Deutsch?
example_sentences.en: How do you say that in German?

example_sentences.de: Wie sagt man das noch mal?
example_sentences.en: How do you say that again?

cloze.en: How do you say that in German?

words.notes: 'man' here means 'one / people in general' — it is not the word for a male person.

example_sentences.en: How do you spell your name?

words.germany_context: You will be asked to spell your name constantly. Learning the German alphabet pays for itself in the first week.

example_sentences.en: I'm looking for the bus stop.

example_sentences.de: Ich suche eine Wohnung in Berlin.
example_sentences.en: I'm looking for a flat in Berlin.

cloze.en: I'm looking for the main station.

words.notes: suchen takes a direct object with no preposition — 'Ich suche die Post', never 'suche für'.
brauchen takes the accusative: 'Ich brauche einen Termin' (not 'ein Termin').

example_sentences.en: I would like to make an appointment.

words.notes: When a second verb follows, it goes to the end in the infinitive: 'Ich möchte einen Termin vereinbaren.'

example_sentences.en: Excuse me, how much is this?
How much does the ticket cost?

words.notes: 'Wie viel kostet das?' means the same thing and is equally common.

words.germany_context: Police is 110. Never call 110 for a medical problem — that is 112.

example_sentences.de: Ich fühle mich nicht gut, ich gehe nach Hause.
example_sentences.en: I don't feel well, I'm going home.

words.notes: 'Mir ist schlecht' specifically means nauseous. 'Ich fühle mich nicht gut' is general.

example_sentences.de: Mein Sohn ist allergisch gegen Milch.
example_sentences.en: My son is allergic to milk.

words.notes: Always 'allergisch gegen' + accusative. Worth memorising before you eat out.

example_sentences.de: Ich habe mein Handy im Zug verloren.
example_sentences.en: I lost my phone on the train.

words.germany_context: Lost property is the Fundbüro. Public transport operators and the Deutsche Bahn each run their own, separate from the city one.

example_sentences.en: Excuse me, where is the station?

cloze.en: Excuse me, may I get past?

words.notes: Use it both to get someone's attention and to apologise. 'Entschuldigen Sie' is the slightly more formal version.

example_sentences.de: Es tut mir leid, ich habe das nicht gewusst.
example_sentences.en: I'm sorry, I didn't know that.

cloze.de: Es tut mir ___, ich komme zu spät.

words.notes: For a genuine apology. 'Entschuldigung' is lighter — for bumping into someone.

example_sentences.de: Einen Moment bitte, ich suche das Formular.
example_sentences.en: One moment please, I'm looking for the form.

example_sentences.de: Moment, ich verstehe das nicht ganz.
example_sentences.en: Hold on, I don't quite understand that.

cloze.en: One moment please, I'm coming right away.

words.notes: Buys you time to think of the next German sentence. Extremely handy.
Very common informal 'OK'. As a question it means 'Are you all right?'

example_sentences.de: Kein Problem, das mache ich gern.
example_sentences.en: No problem, I'm happy to do it.

words.notes: kein negates a noun. 'Problem' is neuter, so it's 'kein Problem'.

example_sentences.de: Ich weiß nicht, wo das ist.
example_sentences.en: I don't know where that is.

cloze.de: Ich ___ nicht, wann der Bus kommt.
cloze.en: I don't know when the bus comes.

words.notes: wissen is for facts; kennen is for being familiar with a person or place.

example_sentences.en: Excuse me, is this seat still free?

cloze.en: Excuse me, is this still free?

words.germany_context: Asked constantly on trains and in busy cafés, where sharing a table with strangers is completely normal.

words.notes: dürfen is about permission. kann is about ability — mixing them up is a classic error.

example_sentences.de: Haben Sie das auch in Größe M?
example_sentences.en: Do you have this in size M too?
Do you have an appointment available?

cloze.en: Do you have this in blue as well?

example_sentences.de: Gibt es hier in der Nähe einen Supermarkt?

words.notes: 'es gibt' is always followed by the accusative: 'Gibt es hier einen Supermarkt?'

example_sentences.de: Wo kann ich eine Fahrkarte kaufen?
example_sentences.en: Where can I buy a ticket?

example_sentences.de: Wo kann ich hier Geld abheben?
example_sentences.en: Where can I withdraw money here?

words.notes: The second verb goes to the very end: 'Wo kann ich eine Fahrkarte kaufen?'

example_sentences.de: Ich bin neu hier und kenne die Stadt noch nicht.
example_sentences.en: I'm new here and don't know the city yet.

cloze.de: Ich bin ___ hier, können Sie mir helfen?
cloze.en: I'm new here, can you help me?

words.notes: Explains your German and gets you more patience. Worth saying early.

example_sentences.de: Ich komme aus der Türkei, aus Istanbul.
Woher kommen Sie? — Ich komme aus Deutschland.
example_sentences.en: Where are you from? — I'm from Germany.

words.notes: Most countries take no article (aus Deutschland, aus Spanien), but a few do: aus der Türkei, aus der Schweiz, aus den USA.

example_sentences.de: Wie heißen Sie? — Ich heiße Müller.
example_sentences.en: What's your name? — My name is Müller.

cloze.en: My name is Emre. And you?

words.notes: 'Mein Name ist…' is also correct and slightly more formal.

example_sentences.en: Excuse me, I'd like to pay.

words.notes: Just 'Zahlen, bitte!' also works and is very common.
words.germany_context: In restaurants you pay at the table, not at a till. The waiter will ask 'Zusammen oder getrennt?' — together or separately. Splitting is completely normal.

example_sentences.de: Kann ich mit Karte zahlen? — Nein, nur Bargeld.
example_sentences.en: Can I pay by card? — No, cash only.

words.germany_context: Germany is still surprisingly cash-heavy. Many bakeries, bars, small restaurants and even doctors are 'nur Bargeld'. Always carry some cash, and note that a German EC-Karte is accepted far more widely than a foreign credit card.

example_sentences.de: Guten Tag, ich habe einen Termin um zehn Uhr.
example_sentences.en: Hello, I have an appointment at ten o'clock.
I'd like to make an appointment.

cloze.en: I have an appointment at 2 pm.

words.germany_context: 'Haben Sie einen Termin?' is the first thing you'll be asked at almost any German office, doctor or bank. Walk-ins are often refused outright — book online well in advance.

words.word: Lassen Sie mich bitte in Ruhe.
words.lemma: Lassen Sie mich bitte in Ruhe

example_sentences.de: Lassen Sie mich bitte in Ruhe!

words.notes: Said firmly, this is understood immediately. Worth knowing even if you hope never to use it.

example_sentences.de: Sonst noch etwas? — Nein, das ist alles.

words.notes: The natural answer to 'Sonst noch etwas?' at any counter.

words.translation: Could you write that down, please?
translations: Could you write that down, please?

example_sentences.de: Können Sie mir das bitte aufschreiben?
example_sentences.en: Could you write that down for me, please?

example_sentences.de: Schreiben Sie bitte die Adresse auf.

cloze.en: Could you write that down, please?

words.notes: aufschreiben is separable: 'Schreiben Sie das bitte auf.' Reading German is much easier than hearing it, so this rescues a lot of conversations.

example_sentences.en: Excuse me, what time is it?

cloze.en: Excuse me, what time is it?

words.notes: 'Wie viel Uhr ist es?' means the same. Careful with the answer: 'halb drei' is 2:30, not 3:30.
